title_en: ICYMI: New Previews of Wolverine, Star Wars: Zero Company, and More!
summary_en: Your one-stop shop for any game preview coverage you might've missed at IGN this week from Marvel's Wolverine, Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave, Star Wars: Zero Company, and Job Simulator: Human Relations.
body_en:
We're rapidly racing towards the holidays (I know it's only August, but in the video game world, "Fall" starts in earnest in August), and that means we've got a ton of big games coming our way over the next few months. Most of them aren't named Grand Theft Auto 6, even! And so we thought we'd start a new weekly roundup of game preview coverage on IGN in case you missed anything over the course of the week. Some heavy hitters stepped up to the plate this week: Marvel's Wolverine, Star Wars: Zero Company, Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave, and Job Simulator: Human Relations. Be sure to click through for the full previews of each game below, and buckle up – it's going to be one heck of a sprint to 2026's finish line in the video game world!
Key Preview Takeaways:
If Insomniac has proved anything over the last eight years, it’s that they know how to make a hell of a superhero game. Spider-Man remains one of the PlayStation 4’s defining action games and a shining example of open-world design, as are both of its follow-ups. Now they’re looking to replicate that magic with Wolverine, albeit this time as a traditional linear AAA action game. I got to play about two and half hours at a recent preview event, and while my impressions are mostly glowingly positive, I did come away with a few questions and concerns.
Check out our full Wolverine preview for more.
Key Preview Takeaways:
As a kid, one of my favourite moments in The Empire Strikes Back was when Han Solo and Chewbacca got the drop on an Imperial probe droid on Hoth by flanking it on either side and blasting it to bits, so you can imagine I was pretty stoked when Star Wars Zero Company allowed me to pull off plenty of ice cold combat manoeuvres just like it during the first 10 hours of its campaign. When it was first revealed last year I assumed this turn-based tactics adventure would only appeal to hardcore fans of the genre, that it was merely XCOM with X-Wings, perhaps. However, after getting hands-on with a near-finished build, I’m happy to report that Zero Company’s strategic shooting seems extremely approachable for newcomers without sacrificing any of the complexity that more experienced fans might expect. It’s a bit like a Sarlacc pit: very easy to drop into, but you might be surprised at just how deep it gets.
Check out our full Star Wars: Zero Company preview for more.
Key Preview Takeaways:
After seven years, Fire Emblem is finally returning to the world introduced in Fire Emblem: Three Houses. There’s a lot of similarities to be found in the structure of Fire Emblem: Fortune’s Weave, but there are also plenty of ways that developer Intelligent Systems is building out the features that defined Three Houses in some pretty exciting ways. Even though I was only able to get just a few chapters in with each of the main heroes, I’ve already found several new additions I’m very fond of… and maybe one that I’m not as high on.
Check out our full Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave preview for more.
Key Preview Takeaways:
It was with plenty of excitement that I sat down recently to play Job Simulator: Human Relations, a non-VR version of the popular comedic multiplayer workplace sim that is played on a regular ol’ flat-screen monitor. Although ironically, your character is an anthropomorphized CRT monitor, walking around each floor of the company office building and trying to manage the increasingly more insane things happening around you.
Check out our full Job Simulator: Human Relations preview for more.
Ryan McCaffrey is IGN's executive editor of previews and host of IGN's weekly Xbox show, Podcast Unlocked , and a co-host of Next-Gen Console Watch . He's a North Jersey guy, so it's "Taylor ham," not "pork roll." Debate it with him on Twitter at @DMC_Ryan .
